overview.summary: A Queue is a linear data structure that follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle.
learningObjectives: Implement a Queue using a Linked List (or dynamic array).
Recognize problems that require sequential processing like BFS.
overview.interviewRelevance: Queues are the backbone of Breadth-First Search (BFS) for trees and graphs, and are essential for scheduling tasks.

paragraphs: Think of a line at a coffee shop. You enter at the back of the line, and you wait your turn.
The first person who got in line is the first person to order and leave. This is FIFO.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: A Queue preserves the exact order of arrival. It's the ultimate 'fair' data structure.

definition.technicalDefinition: A Queue is an abstract data type that serves as a collection of elements, with two principal operations: enqueue (adds to the back) and dequeue (removes from the front).

vocabulary.definition: Insert an element at the back (tail) of the queue.
Remove the element at the front (head) of the queue.
Look at the first element without removing it.

keyProperties: O(n) search (since you only have direct access to the front).
Best implemented with a Linked List to avoid O(n) shifting.

metaphor: A car wash tunnel. Cars enter one side and exit the other side in the exact same order.
mentalModel.clickSentence: Use a Queue whenever you need to process things in the exact order they were discovered.

memoryDescription: Implementing a Queue with a standard Array is bad because removing the first element requires shifting all other elements (O(n)).
Instead, Queues are usually implemented using a Doubly Linked List, where enqueueing at the tail and dequeueing at the head are both O(1).

definitionCode.python:
from collections import deque
q = deque()
q.append(1)    # Enqueue
front = q.popleft() # Dequeue

code.python:
q = deque()
q.append(x)      # enqueue at back
q.popleft()      # dequeue from front

steps.explanation: A queue is first-in, first-out, like a line at a ticket counter. L marks the front, R the back.
dequeue(): A was first in, so it leaves first.
dequeue(): B was first in, so it leaves first.

operations.name: Enqueue
operations.description: Add an item to the back of the queue.
operations.visualNote: A new element enters the back of the line.

operations.name: Dequeue
operations.visualNote: The front element exits the line.

patternTemplate.pseudocode:
q = new Queue()
q.enqueue(start_node)
while not q.is_empty():
  curr = q.dequeue()
  process(curr)
  for neighbor in curr.neighbors:
    q.enqueue(neighbor)
patternTemplate.whenToUse: Whenever you need to process data level-by-level, or maintain fairness (First come, first served).

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You are building a customer support ticket system where the oldest tickets must be answered first.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: Oldest first means First-In-First-Out (FIFO). This is the textbook definition of a Queue.

examples.title: Number of Recent Calls
examples.problemStatement: Count the number of requests that happened in the past 3000 milliseconds.
steps: Store all pings in a Queue.
When a new ping arrives, enqueue its timestamp.
While the front of the queue is older than (current_ping - 3000), dequeue it.
Return the size of the queue.
examples.spaceComplexity: O(W) where W is the window size
examples.rationale: Since time always moves forward, the oldest pings will always be at the front of the queue, making them easy to discard.

conceptQuiz.question: Which principle does a Queue follow?
conceptQuiz.explanation: FIFO. The first item to enter the queue is the first one to leave.

conceptQuiz.question: Why is implementing a Queue with a standard array usually bad?
options: Dequeueing from the front requires shifting all other elements O(n).
Arrays cannot store dynamic data types.
conceptQuiz.explanation: If you remove index 0, index 1 must move to index 0, index 2 to index 1, etc. This is O(n) time. Linked Lists can dequeue in O(1).

practice.title: Number of Recent Calls
practice.keyInsight: Use a queue to track the rolling 3000ms window.

practice.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
practice.keyInsight: Use two stacks: one for pushing, one for popping/peeking.
